text:
camille: Heads-up — canary for the new system-prompt change shows warmup hit-rate collapse on the prefix cache. Yesterday baseline ~78%, canary down to ~34%.

drew: ouch. which commit and model variant?

camille: rollout id rl/2026-03-17/sys-prompt-v2 -> redwood/gpt-medium-quant@v3. tokenizer bumped toklib 0.9.2 in same deploy (we probably shouldn't have).

mia: do you have the profiler traces? kernel selection or batching could explain latency but hit-rate suggests key mismatch.

camille: attaching quick numbers from the warmup job: 
```
warmup-run: 2026-03-17T21:04Z
prefix_hits: 34
prefix_misses: 66
avg_kv_fetch_ms: 28
avg_first_token_ms: 132
batch_size_p50: 8
```

kevin: that avg_first_token spike + hit-rate drop smells like KV miss + expensive kernel fallback (longer seq path). any stack traces?

runtime-bot: deploy rl/2026-03-17/sys-prompt-v2 started on dedicated-pool-3 (region-us-west)

arnav: quick hypothesis: tokenizer hash for keys changed (token ids different between toklib 0.9.1 and 0.9.2). If cache key uses tokenized prefix + raw prompt, any token-level diff will break keys.

mia: can we confirm by canonicalizing keys on the warmup job side? run a transformation that uses `normalized_text = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', prompt).strip()` then `tokens = tokenizer.encode(normalized_text, version='pin-0.9.1')` and compute key hash. If that restores hits we know culprit.

camille: I ran a quick AB on a few hundred prefixes: when we force `version=0.9.1` for tokenization in the warmup harness, hit-rate goes to 76%. So tokenizer drift is main offender.

drew: nice find. we need a mitigation that doesn't force downgrades broadly. Options: 1) pin tokenizer version in cache key generation (explicit field), 2) move to text-normalized-only key (avoid token ids entirely), 3) embed tokenizer version into key metadata and provide compat mapping.

kevin: tradeoffs: token-id-based keys are compact and avoid ambiguous text normalization quirks (whitespace, quoting). Text-only keys are larger and slower to compare. Also kernel selection logic currently optimizes for canonical key length; changing it could affect batching heuristics.

mia: suggestion: adopt a canonical key tuple: `[model_family, tokenizer_version, normalized_text_v1]` where `normalized_text_v1` uses NFKC, collapse whitespace, JSON-serialize tool/function fields with `sort_keys=True` and remove ephemeral fields (trace_id, timestamp). That keeps tokenizer version explicit and makes keys deterministic.

arnav: +1 on deterministic serialization for tool calls. Current bug: tool arg order sometimes differs (user-provided dict vs ordered list) and we include raw JSON in the prefix; that was nuking matches. Example quick fix: `json.dumps(tool_payload, separators=(
,:
), sort_keys=True)` then hash.

camille: I like that. also propose an automatic warmup step after any tokenizer or system-prompt change that primes the KV cache for high-volume prefixes (small job over historical prompt corpus). If runtime detects tokenizer_version change it triggers warmup job and routes traffic to fallback until hit-rate recovers.

drew: ops question: how long to warm up for typical suffix distributions? earlier warmup jobs ran for 30m and got ~85% coverage for our top-200 prefixes. With tokenizer drift we may need to re-run incrementally.

kevin: we should add a metric `cache_key_version` to the telemetry so we can correlate hit-rates with key-serialization scheme. Also add a gating check in deploy: if `cache_key_schema` or `tokenizer` changes, require explicit warmup approval or automated warmup run.

mia: quick patch plan:
- runtime: add `tokenizer_version` into cache key builder (non-breaking, default to current runtime pin)
- data-plane: canonicalize tool/function payloads via sorted JSON and strip ephemeral fields
- control-plane: on schema/tokenizer change, enqueue warmup job and delay full rollout until hit-rate > 70% or 15m elapsed

arnav: will prototype `key_builder.canonicalize(tool_obj)` and include unit tests for ordering/stripping. Also add fuzzy compare util to detect accidental key drift in CI by replaying example prefixes.

camille: thanks — can we get an owner for the deploy gating? who can add the control-plane check? @drew?

drew: ok I can add the gating check and metric plumbing. will coordinate with @arnav and @kevin for runtime changes.

kevin: I'll look at kernel selection fallout — if we see fallback to slow kernels on misses, we can short-circuit to faster approximate kernels during warmup to reduce tail latency.

camille: super. follow-ups: 1) patch for canonical key PRs (arnav, kevin), 2) gating change (drew), 3) warmup job template + corpus (camille/mia). I'll open a thread in eng-runtime with the plan and link the PRs. :thumbsup:

runtime-bot: incident-note logged: INC-2026-03-17-prefix-warmup-regression (assigned: camille)

mia: one more note — keep an eye on model rollbacks too. if we re-roll tokenizer quickly make sure warmup is happy path in the rollback flow.

camille: noted. I'll post PR links when ready.
